catalogue_requests.reason: cap.actuation.valve.v1 binds actuation.valve/fluid.valve and takes outlet/state/position; this process.controller command takes an olfactometer valve number (1 to 8) and an open/closed state, and no catalogue class binds a numbered olfactometer valve on process.controller.
No catalogue class expresses the upstream eight-character binary valve pattern (leftmost character is Valve 1); the runtime schema needs the pattern constraint and an array of valve states.
cap.actuation.gpio.v1 binds io.gpio/io.digital, not process.controller, and its mode/value model does not match the upstream set_gpio(pin, mode) command with the fixed high/low modes.
No catalogue class covers starting the Teensy camera trigger on a process.controller; the upstream command sends a fixed begin sequence and the driver leaves the frame rate at the upstream default.
No catalogue class covers stopping the Teensy camera trigger on a process.controller.

No catalogue class expresses the composite safe state of this rig (laser off, all eight olfactometer valves closed, camera trigger stopped); a safe_state=True action must take no input and report that the commands were sent.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card lists helper PythonObjectDriver, but nebPod.Controller builds each serial command from parts (a command letter, a subcommand letter and integers) and exposes no plain command table, so this is a direct decorated Driver over nebPod:Controller with a native.py factory (driver-authoring.md, 'Choosing the shape'); the card's decision direct-driver and the entry symbol nebPod:Controller are unchanged. The driver is hardware mode R2 because the upstream commands a Cobalt laser; @estop calls the upstream turn_off_laser(0), and the safe_state=True action also closes all eight olfactometer valves and stops the camera trigger. No hardware backend was run and no human reviewed or tested the package; reviewed_by stays null. The upstream class has no state query (block_until_read only waits for one reply byte), so the four @read parameters report the driver's last commanded state, not a measurement; facts.md says so. Not covered: laser-power measurement and auto-calibration (Thorlabs photometer and calibration table), SpikeGLX recording control and the gate/run-name helpers, Hering-Breuer/tone/TTL/gas-valve commands, GPIO pulse mode (no sourced pulse-width range), and the camera frame-rate input (the action uses the upstream default). No numeric bound needed an operator overlay, so site-limits.example.json is not present. The fake is an in-memory stand-in; the gate evidence is contract_checked.
